{"type":"text","timestamp":1794623378715,"sessionID":"ses_e281e379fffeS1QHbAT7SAvLQQ","part":{"id":"prt_1d7e39511001VHmJXx012ooQXk","messageID":"msg_1d7e37903001f8QzJa4tYvufqy","sessionID":"ses_e281e379fffeS1QHbAT7SAvLQQ","type":"text","text":"The episode is over, and the score is almost certainly 0. The rover ran out of battery in the last few ticks.\n\n**What went right:**\n- I sampled all 7 targets (t1–t5, plus d1 and d2, which appeared during the mission). Six were on time; d1 was late and earned 0.25 of its value.\n- The rover got back to base at tick 25 and stopped about 0.11 m from it, inside the 0.75 m radius. Without the battery problem that would have been 9.5 of 12 value, a score of about 0.79.\n- Wheel slip on bedrock was 1–5%, and I adjusted each drive for it using the telemetry.\n\n**What went wrong:** I never checked the whole route against the battery. I planned for the deadlines and the distances, but forgot to set aside enough charge for the time left after returning to base. Every tick costs 0.5 energy even when the rover is parked. It reached base with 11.53 energy, and the 25 ticks still to run needed 12.5. The last telemetry packet I received (tick 47) showed 0.53, so the battery hit zero around tick 49. When I spotted this at tick 24, the remaining moves were already queued and there's no way to cancel commands.\n\n**What would have avoided it:** Skipping the late d1 sample (worth only 0.5) would have saved roughly 9 energy: 3 for the sample and about 6 for the extra driving. The rover would then have ended at base with energy to spare and a score of about 0.75. Next time I should check the energy budget, including all the idle ticks after returning to base, before committing to each detour.","time":{"start":1794623378705,"end":1794623378713}}}
